requirement: Classification shall use the **Library of Congress Classification** scheme, not Dewey. HOL uses LCC.
A call number is shared by all copies of a title; an **accession number is unique to one physical copy**. Three copies of a title share a class number and hold three different accession numbers.
Shelf location shall be derived from the call number's LCC letter: classes **A–J are in the South wing**, classes **K–Z are in the North wing**.
Not every item circulates. Reference, serials, on-display and restricted collections shall not be borrowable.
Borrowing privileges shall vary by member category. HOL grants postgraduates and senior staff access that undergraduates do not have.
Membership shall originate in person. Users present a university identity card and library card and sign a register. The system shall not offer public self-registration.

The catalogue shall provide **at least three access points — author, title and subject** — mirroring the card catalogue and HOL's OPAC, which searches "author, title and subject entries, keywords in titles".
Borrowing history shall be preserved after return. A returned loan is closed, never deleted.
Member identity and borrowing history are personal data under Nigerian data protection law. A borrowing history is a reading-habits profile and shall be treated as sensitive.
A member shall log in with their matriculation/staff ID or university email, plus a password.
The system shall not provide public self-registration. Accounts are created by staff only. (DOM-006)
A user shall change their own password by supplying the current password.
A user shall request a password reset, delivered as a link to their registered email.
A password reset token shall be single-use and expire within 30 minutes.
A user shall log out, invalidating their refresh token.
A user created by staff shall be required to change their password at first login.
The system shall assign every account exactly one role: `member`, `librarian` or `admin`.
A librarian shall create a member record with name, ID, email and category.
A librarian shall bulk-import members from a CSV file.
The CSV import shall report per-row success and failure without aborting the whole batch.
A librarian shall search and list members.
A librarian shall view a member's profile including current loans and full history.
A librarian shall update a member record.
A librarian shall suspend or reactivate a member. A suspended member cannot borrow.
A librarian shall create a book record: title, author(s), ISBN, publisher, place and year of publication, LCC call number, subject headings, description.
A librarian shall import bibliographic data from an external book API by ISBN to pre-fill a new record. (DEC-007)
Imported data shall be editable before saving; the librarian's entry is authoritative.
A librarian shall update a book record.
A librarian shall archive a book. Archived books leave search results but their loan history is preserved. (DOM-008)
A librarian shall manage subject headings and LCC categories.
A librarian shall add a copy to a book, recording a **unique accession number**. (DOM-002)
The system shall reject a duplicate accession number.
Each copy shall carry a loan policy: `circulating`, `reference_only`, `on_display` or `restricted`. (DOM-004)
Each copy shall carry a status: `available`, `on_loan`, `lost`, `damaged` or `withdrawn`.
A librarian shall mark a copy lost, damaged or withdrawn, removing it from circulation without deleting its history.
The system shall derive and display a copy's wing from its call number. (DOM-003)
A user shall search the catalogue by **title**. (DOM-007)
A user shall search by **author**. (DOM-007)
A user shall search by **subject**. (DOM-007)
A user shall search by free-text keyword across title, author and subject.
A user shall search by ISBN.
A user shall search by call number.
A user shall filter results by LCC category and by availability.
Search results shall be paginated.
A user shall view a book's detail page showing bibliographic data, copy counts, availability and shelf location.
Search shall be available to unauthenticated visitors; personal data shall not be.
The system shall report, per book, the total number of copies, the number available and the number on loan.
Availability shall be **derived from copy states**, never stored as a standalone flag.
Non-circulating copies shall be reported as held by the library but not available to borrow. (DOM-004)
A librarian shall record a loan of a specific copy to a specific member.
The system shall compute the due date from the member's category. (DEC-005)
The system shall reject a loan that would exceed the member's category limit.
The system shall reject a loan of a non-circulating copy. (DOM-004)
The system shall reject a loan to a suspended or inactive member.
The system shall reject a loan of a copy that is not `available`.
Concurrent attempts to lend the same copy shall result in exactly one successful loan.
A librarian shall record the return of a borrowed copy.
Recording a return shall set the loan's return date and close its status.
Recording a return shall restore the copy to `available`.
The system shall reject a return for a loan that is already closed.
The system shall identify loans whose due date has passed and which are unreturned.
Overdue status shall be **computed**, not stored, so it cannot go stale.
A librarian shall list all overdue loans, filterable by member and by book.
A member shall reserve a book whose copies are all on loan, or which is on display.
Reservations shall be queued in order of request.
A member shall view and cancel their own reservations.
When a copy becomes available, the system shall notify the member at the head of the queue.
An unclaimed reservation shall expire after a configurable period and pass to the next in queue.
A member shall view the books they currently hold, with due dates.
A member shall view their own complete borrowing history.
A member shall not view any other member's history. (DOM-009)
A librarian shall view the full loan history of any member or any copy.
Loan records shall be immutable once closed. (DOM-008)
A librarian shall view a dashboard: total books, total copies, active loans, overdue count, members.
A librarian shall view most-borrowed titles over a period.
An administrator shall create and manage librarian accounts.
The system shall record an audit log of staff actions on catalogue, members and loans.
The system shall notify a member by email before a loan falls due.
The system shall notify a member when a loan becomes overdue.
The system shall support push notification via Firebase Cloud Messaging.
Notifications shall be queued and delivered asynchronously, never blocking an API response.
The system shall publish an OpenAPI 3 specification and serve interactive Swagger documentation.
The system shall expose a health endpoint reporting service and database reachability.
Search response time: 95th percentile under 500 ms for a 10,000-book catalogue at 50 concurrent users
Password storage: Argon2id, unique salt per password. Plaintext or unsalted hashes are a defect.
Session tokens: JWT access token expiring in 15 minutes; refresh token in 7 days and revocable
Access control: Role checked server-side on every protected endpoint. Client-side checks are not access control.
Brute-force resistance: Authentication endpoints rate-limited to 5 attempts per minute per IP
Transport: HTTPS only, HSTS enabled, HTTP redirected
Input validation: Every request body and query parameter validated server-side before use
Injection resistance: Parameterised queries exclusively. No string-concatenated SQL.
Data integrity: `available_copies` shall never be negative and loans shall never exceed total copies. Enforced by database constraint and transaction, not application code alone.
Logging: Structured logs. No passwords, tokens or member personal data written to logs. (DOM-009)
Container size: Final Docker image under 50 MB via multi-stage build on a distroless or scratch base
Test coverage: At least 70% statement coverage on business-logic packages
Continuous integration: Every push runs build, vet, lint and the full test suite. A red build blocks merge.
API documentation: Every endpoint documented in OpenAPI 3 with request, response and error shapes
Secret management: All secrets supplied by environment variable. No credential committed to version control.
CORS: Restricted to known frontend origins. Wildcard origins are a defect.
Error handling: Uniform error envelope. Stack traces and driver errors never returned to clients.
Portability: Runs from a single container image with no host-specific configuration
Accessibility support: API supplies the text alternatives, labels and semantic data the frontend needs for WCAG compliance
Auditability: Every state-changing staff action attributable to an account and a timestamp
